title: Private control plane hardening, terraform notes, and upgrade scrub log
content:
Purpose
This is a compact runbook and working notes document focused on three things: 1) hardening steps that must be applied prior to any major control-plane upgrade, 2) Terraform module notes and recommended usage patterns for on-prem/VPC installs, and 3) a reusable upgrade 'scrub' and verification log that operators should iterate on during canary and full rollouts. Treat this document as the source of operator checklists and ephemeral logs for any private-controlplane upgrade where downtime must be minimized.

Scope and assumptions
- Applies to Private Control Plane (PCP) v0.9.x -> v1.x major upgrades in VPC and air-gapped on-prem installs.
- Assumes customer infra provides: managed PostgreSQL or self-hosted Postgres cluster, KMS (cloud or HSM), and Kubernetes 1.24+ or equivalent container runtime.
- Assumes Terraform-based provisioning for infra and Helm for chart installs.
- This doc is not a full security design review. Perform a separate compliance pass for regulated customers.

High-level upgrade phases (for patch and minor upgrades)
1) Preflight & hardening sweep (2-6 hours)
   - Confirm backups for Postgres, KMS metadata, and any object-store snapshots exist and are retrievable. Note snapshot IDs in the scrub log.
   - Rotate ephemeral credentials used by CI and operator accounts to avoid leaked keys during ops.
   - Verify RBAC least privilege for service accounts in the PCP namespace. List any elevated roles and re-evaluate.
   - Run tf plan with -destroy=false and -detailed-exitcode to detect drift.

2) Canary rollout (1-3 hours)
   - Deploy new control-plane artifacts in a canary zone/cluster with traffic split ~5-10%.
   - Run end-to-end smoke tests and tokenized request load (see Tests section).

3) Full rollout and post-verify (2-6 hours)
   - Gradual scaling to 25%/50%/100% traffic with automated health checks.
   - Post-upgrade regression checks and quality gating.

Preflight & hardening checklist (detailed)
- Backups & recovery
  - Postgres: create base backup and a WAL archive point. Backup ID and retention verified.
  - Object store: snapshot control-plane S3 bucket (or local equivalent) to a read-only path.
  - KMS/HSM: export current public keys and key metadata (do not export private keys). Record key versions.

- Secrets and certs
  - Check certificate expiry for TLS between components (controlplane -> datastore, controlplane -> agents, operator UI). Replace any certificate expiring within 90 days.
  - Validate K8s secrets usage: ensure no plaintext secrets in helm charts or values.yaml.

- Network hardening
  - Ensure private subnets used by PCP are behind a firewall with egress rules restricted to necessary artifact repos and monitoring endpoints.
  - For air-gapped installs, validate mirror registry hashes and signed SBOMs for each image.

Terraform module notes (practical guidance)
- Module layout conventions
  - Keep three top-level modules per customer: network (vpc, subnets, nsg), infra (datastore, kms, object-store), controlplane (k8s resources, helm).
  - Use inputs.tf to expose a minimal surface area: region, cidr_block, postgres_uri, kms_config, image_registry. Avoid passing long lists of internal resource IDs.

- State management
  - Use remote state backend (S3/GCS) with encryption and state locking (DynamoDB for AWS).
  - Split state per module: network.tfstate, infra.tfstate, controlplane.tfstate. This lets us apply controlplane changes without network-level lock contention.

- Versioning and upgrade path
  - Pin module versions with git tags and create a release changelog. Keep a migration submodule for breaking changes that perform api-compatible transformations (e.g., secret name changes).

Example minimal usage (HCL snippet)
- Note: placeholder only, do not paste private values into Drive.
module "controlplane" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/private-controlplane-modules.git//controlplane?ref=v1.0.0"
  k8s_cluster_id = var.k8s_cluster_id
  postgres_uri   = var.postgres_uri
  kms_config     = var.kms_config
  image_registry = var.image_registry
}

Upgrade scrub log template (operators should fill fields during run)
- Upgrade ID: <YYYYMMDD-identifier>
- Operator on-call: <name, pager>
- Customer/Cluster: <tenant-id or cluster-name>
- Preflight checks completed: [yes/no], timestamp
- Backup IDs: [postgres: id], [s3: id], [snapshot: id]
- Terraform plan summary: <short text or plan hash>
- Canary start: timestamp
- Canary pass/fail: <pass/fail> and notes
- Rollout increments: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with timestamps and health metrics
- Post-verify checks: e2e result hash, latency percentiles, error rates
- Rollback performed: [yes/no], rollback-id, reason
- Postmortem notes: short bullets of what went wrong and follow-up tickets

Canary + smoke tests (executable checklist)
- Health endpoints: /healthz for each control-plane pod must return 200 and JSON {"status":"ok"}.
- KV-cache warmup: send warmup queries to build KV caches for common model families (gpt-style, decoder-only). Observe cache-hit metric increases.
- Token-throughput sanity: run a 1-minute token generator at 50 qps and verify p50 < configured SLO and p99 within acceptable bounds.
- Auth smoke: simulate token-based requests and validate RBAC-enforced routes.

Rollbacks and partial rollback patterns
- Fast rollback (config or image revert): reapply previous Helm release or promote previous image tag; do not delete new schema migrations automatically.
- DB-sensitive rollback: if a migration was applied, follow the migration reverse plan in the migration ticket. Prefer forward-fix over backward migration when customer data risk is high.

KMS and key rotation notes
- Never rotate primary KMS key until post-verify pass. Use key aliasing (alias/current, alias/next) to enable staged rotation.
- For HSM customers, co-ordinate with their security contact and record HSM audit IDs in the scrub log.
- During rotation, ensure token signing and verification endpoints accept both old and new key versions for a rolling period.

Database migration guidance
- Use zero-downtime migration patterns where possible: create new columns, backfill, switch reads, then drop old columns in a later release.
- Test migration on a full-sized staging snapshot. Time backups and apply migration to estimate outage windows.

Air-gapped specific notes
- Artifact promotion: ensure signed manifests and digests are included. Keep an offline mirror checklist and the target registry digest mapping.
- OOB update channel: provide a signed tarball and idempotent apply script. Test apply script on an isolated host with no internet.

Observed gotchas (operational history)
- Vault/Secrets mount race: on first startup after upgrade, secrets-provisioner may race with helm hooks, causing pods to crash-loop. Workaround: pre-seed secrets or add 30s post-install wait in Helm hooks for sensitive components.
- Postgres schema drift between minor patched nodes: always run schema-sync step and verify version file in migrations table.
- Image registry auth tokens expiring mid-rollout: ensure CI short-lived tokens are refreshed and accessible from operator terminal during long upgrades.

Post-upgrade verification and metrics to capture
- Latency p50/p95/p99 for control-plane routes pre- and post-upgrade (compare to baseline).
- Error rate (5xx) and business-level errors (auth, rate-limit exceeds).
- CPU/GPU memory consumption and pod restart counts.
- KV cache hit ratio and number of cold-cache evictions during first 30 minutes.

Maintenance window template (communicating externally)
- Planned window: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM to HH:MM (UTC)
- Expected impact: brief request degradation for up to N minutes during canary migration; full failover negligible.
- Contact: on-call + escalation contact.
- Post-upgrade status: link to scrub log and verification report.

Follow-ups and tickets to open (example)
- CP-zzz: add pre-install hook to seed KMS alias mapping.
- CP-yyy: add terraform remote-state remediation for race conditions.
- CP-xxx: automate canary traffic split and metric-based promotion.

Appendix: quick commands and snippets
- Terraform plan with detailed exit codes:
  terraform init -backend-config=... && terraform plan -detailed-exitcode -out=plan.tfplan
- Apply with targeted state and locking: apply controlplane state only\  terraform apply -target=module.controlplane plan.tfplan
- Helm rollback:
  helm history redwood-controlplane -n redwood && helm rollback redwood-controlplane <REV> -n redwood

Operator notes (recent run)
- Upgrade ID: 20260220-cp-hardening-test
- Operator: Maya Chen
- Summary: Canary failed initially due to missing cert rotation; applied cert refresh and retried. Full rollout completed with a single 20m blip in token latency p95. Follow-up: CP-542 to ensure helm hooks are tolerant to secret provisioning delays.

End of document.
